A prev
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts, repair a corrupted regex-escape call on line 3787.

A previous edit to this line was applied incorrectly: the anchor text of that edit was substituted into the replacement argument where the escape placeholder should have been. The file now contains exactly one occurrence of this fragment:
base.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\\]\]/g, "\\if (grounding.includes(base)) continue; // visible in the window → groundable, fine")

Replace that fragment with exactly this:
base.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, (c) => "\\" + c)

One file, one op. Everything else on the line, including the surrounding new RegExp(...) call, the leading "/", the trailing "(?![A-Za-z0-9])", the .test(grounding) and the trailing comment, stays exactly as it is.

WHY. The intent of that call is to escape regex metacharacters in a filename before embedding it in a RegExp. As it stands, two things are wrong. The character class reads [.*+?^${}()|[\\]\] which matches a metacharacter only when it is immediately followed by a right square bracket, and the replacement is a long literal sentence rather than the matched character. For ordinary basenames nothing matches, so the call is currently a no-op and the surrounding check behaves correctly by accident; but a filename containing a bracket would splice that entire sentence into the pattern.

The replacement uses a function replacer, (c) => "\\" + c, rather than the $& placeholder. That is deliberate: $& is what was misread as a substitution slot last time, and a function replacer cannot be confused for one.

Verified by execution against a grounding window containing learning-signal-health-observer.ts and operational-state.ts. The new form returns false for basename learning-signal-health-observer.t, true for learning-signal-health-observer.ts, false for state.ts, and true for operational-state.ts, which is correct in all four cases, and it does not throw for the bracket-bearing names weird].ts and a.b].ts or for x+y.ts.
